  - other non-live persistent train data already on the entity
- **`is_unidentified` writer.** The runtime sets `is_unidentified = True` at creation, and the one thing that clears it is `SimulationController.adopt_unidentified_train(...)`. It is the predicate every rule about unidentified trains tests — see **Power**, Unidentified trains.
- **Route assignment is not a `Train` field.** Consumers ask `RouteExecutor.assigned_route_id_for(train_id)`. That call prefers the live `RouteExecutor.execution_state_for(train_id).route_id` (the derived RUNNING-`RouteRun` read, not a stored dict — see **Route-run state**), and falls back to scanning `Route.assigned_train_ids` in the route registry (at most one route holds the train, per the single-assignment rule in **Route assignment writers**). The active route is structurally encoded by the live `RouteRun` in `execution_states`, so no per-train sync is needed.
- All live runtime state lives on `TrainController`: `current_span` (live physical span, including end locators and ordered occupied tiles), `current_speed_kmh`, operational `state`, power/cab, ATO/path projections, and operational diagnostics. `TrainPhysics` computes movement and sends `span_update` deltas to the controller, and the controller applies those updates to its own storage. Live target speed and speed-limit reason are reads from controller lookahead at distance 0. There is no `manual_target_speed`, `train.state`, `train.assigned_path_id`, `train.ato_destination_block_id`, `train.current_path`, `train.path_index`, or `train.reserved_blocks` field.
- Initial placement of `TrainController.physics_sync.current_span` is owned by `SimulationController.add_train(...)`. It constructs the train, builds the train's initial physical span from the placement input (reusing the repo's placement-to-position derivation, which produces precise `end_a` / `end_b` locators plus `occupied_tiles`), obtains the controller, and writes the span directly into `TrainController.physics_sync.current_span` before any simulation tick runs. When the placement input names a `RosterEntry` (see **Train Roster**), `add_train(...)` seeds the new `Train`'s persistent fields and its `SpeedProfile` from that entry; without one it builds the train from blank persistent defaults and seeds the default `SpeedProfile` described in **SpeedProfile**. `SimulationController.get_or_create_controller(train_id)` does NOT seed the span; it only makes sure the controller object exists and is registered. There is no parallel `seed_train_span(...)` helper: `add_train(...)` is the one path that seeds `current_span`. Runtime-state save/load is Out of Scope (see the **Out of Scope** section), so no restore path seeds a span either — layout loading rebuilds a `Train` from its persistent config only and does not carry live position.
- An **unidentified train** is the one `Train` the runtime builds for itself rather than through `SimulationController.add_train(...)`: Observe's layout-wide detector snapshot creates it when a block reads current that no existing train accounts for. It is built from blank persistent train defaults with the default `SpeedProfile`, and that profile is never used because an unidentified train is never powered. Its full contract is in **Power**, Unidentified trains.
- After initial placement, `TrainPhysics` is the only normal producer of movement `span_update` values, and `TrainController.on_physics_updated(span_update)` is the only normal writer of `TrainController.physics_sync.current_span`. Two carve-outs mutate the stored span outside that write: Observe's `TrainPhysics.reconcile_to_detected_occupancy(...)` correction (see **Power**, Physical detection outranks the calculated position), and the cab writers' **Reversed-frame re-expression** (see the **TrainSpan schema**), which rewrites only the two end locators' frames when a cab write moves the head to the other physical end. Live movement updates write no position, span, speed, or authority field back to `Train`; the two maintenance counters named in **Maintenance counters** (`total_distance_cm`, `total_run_time_seconds`) are the only `Train` fields `TrainPhysics.tick(...)` writes.


## TrainController

`TrainController` is a multi-module train computer that mirrors a real cab and on-board control system. There is one per train. Inside, it is made of 10 separate sub-modules organized into three layers: input, compute, and output. Code that touches one sub-module must not need to load the others.

**Sub-modules and where to find them in this chapter.**

*Input layer — data feeds into the controller:*

- **Operator command surface** — queue and drain order plus the setter / queue methods themselves: `controller.commands.set_cab(...)`, `controller.commands.set_mode(...)`, `controller.commands.set_manual_mode_type(...)`, `controller.commands.set_handle(...)`, `controller.commands.set_manual_power_percent(...)`, `controller.commands.power_on_cmd()`, `controller.commands.power_off_cmd()`, `controller.commands.enqueue_command(...)`, and `controller.commands.clear_cab()` (the cab-owned ungated clear used only by `TrainController.complete_power_off()` during OFF cleanup — it sets `cab = None` with no gate, is not an operator command, and is never queued, distinct from the precondition-gated `set_cab(...)`; when that write moves the head to the other physical end it applies the **Reversed-frame re-expression** per the **TrainSpan schema**, the same as any other cab writer), plus `controller.eb.activate()` and `controller.eb.release()`. Lives in `train_controller/commands.py` (class `OperatorCommands`); the operator-command queue and drain order are stored on this sub-module and accessed externally as `controller.commands.command_inbox` and `controller.commands.drain_order`. The cab and mode selections it sets are also stored on this sub-module and accessed externally as `controller.commands.cab` and `controller.commands.control_mode` per the **Controller retained field schema** (serialized under the keys `"cab"` and `"control_mode"`). The setter / queue methods orchestrate writes across multiple sub-modules (eb, ato, manual, route_hooks, physics_sync, ops) through the controller back-reference. See **Power/cab/mode command contracts** and **Driver/operator inputs** below.
- **Path plan projection** — live read-only projection of the dispatcher-owned `Path` into `received_path_plan`. Lives in `train_controller/path_projection.py` (class `PathProjection`). No owned fields — every read recomputes from `path_dispatcher.get_active_path(train_id)` (or other live sources) and auto-flips to `None` when the dispatcher transitions the path away from `ACTIVE`. Accessed externally as `controller.path_projection.received_path_plan`, `controller.path_projection.assigned_path_id`, `controller.path_projection.ato_path_id`, `controller.path_projection.ato_destination_block_id`, and `controller.path_projection.get_live_path_data()`. See **received_path_plan schema**, **Dispatcher/route-executor inputs**, and **route/dispatcher command contracts** below.
- **Physics sync** — `current_span` and `current_speed_kmh` storage; `on_physics_updated()` handler; `ControllerProgressReport` generation. Lives in `train_controller/physics_sync.py` (class `PhysicsSync`). It owns the progress mailbox, the named within-tick `pending_detected_entered_blocks: Set[str]` / `pending_detected_vacated_blocks: Set[str]` written in Observe and consumed/cleared by the final Observe callback on a running pass or by `TrainController.build_detected_progress_report()` on a stopped pass, and `pending_block_exit_edges`. `TrainPhysics.reconcile_to_detected_occupancy(train, controller)` writes the Observe synchronous span correction directly onto this sub-module's `current_span` before Plan; there is no separate forward-snap buffer and no `TrainController`-owned intermediary method. The orchestrator methods stay flat on the façade because the runtime and physics invoke them directly.
- **Route hooks** — the controller-transition commands the Action transition-consumer steps call (`depart()`, `enter_station_dwell()`, `finish_dwell()`), plus the seven Action retained latches bundled under `PhaseLatches` that Plan writes and Action consumes. Lives in `train_controller/route_hooks.py` (class `RouteHooks`). Accessed externally as `controller.route_hooks.phase_latches` (and the `set_*` writer helpers on that aggregate per the **Latch Table**). The transition-command methods (`depart`, `enter_station_dwell`, `finish_dwell`) stay flat on the façade because they are the direct commands the Action consumers call; route code writes the matching request latch instead of calling them. See **route/dispatcher command contracts** and **Completion ownership and timing** below.

*Compute layer — the on-board computers:*

- **Operational state machine** — `state` field and transitions (`OFF` / `READY` / `RUNNING_MOVING` / `RUNNING_AT_STATION`) plus the controller-owned `service_stop_active` latch. Lives in `train_controller/ops.py` (class `OperationalStateMachine`); accessed externally as `controller.ops.state`, `controller.ops.service_stop_active`, and `controller.ops.handle_position`. State-transition methods, `TrainController.begin_service_stop()` / `consume_service_stop()`, the canonical stopped predicate `is_stopped()`, and related predicates stay on the façade because they orchestrate writes across multiple sub-modules. See **Controller state machine**, **Controller tick order**, the **Latch Table**, and the **Allowed `(state, cab)` pairs** table.
- **ATC Computer** — live `lookahead` computation, ATC speed-limit application, overspeed-to-EB escalation. Lives in `train_controller/atc.py` (class `ATCComputer`); accessed externally as `controller.atc.safety_margin_cm` (the `track_end_safety_margin_cm` field in **Runtime settings**) and `controller.atc.signal_lookahead_blocks` (the `atc_signal_lookahead_blocks` field in **Runtime settings**; scan depth). `controller.atc.clearance_ahead()`, `controller.atc.speed_limit_now()`, `controller.atc.speed_limit_with_code()`, `controller.atc.is_caution_ahead()`, `controller.atc.is_approaching_yellow_signal()`, `controller.atc.is_signal_red_for_block(block_id)`, and `controller.atc.effective_safety_margin()` are ATC-internal recompute helpers used to build the lookahead payload; they are not an external read surface, and no consumer outside `train_controller/atc.py` calls them for a target speed or reason code — the **canonical lookahead payload** is the single source of truth for that. The canonical lookahead payload is built by `TrainController.get_lookahead()` (`_compute_canonical_lookahead_impl`); `LookaheadBuilder` in `lookahead_builder.py` builds the per-block `LookaheadPoint` list projection. The sub-module also holds four per-tick computation caches — `clearance_ahead_cm`, `speed_limit`, `current_block_speed_limit`, and `_last_limit_reason_code` — that `produce_physics_command()` overwrites at the start of every tick from the freshly computed lookahead, before anything reads them, so they never carry a value across ticks. They exist so the tick body, the overspeed-to-EB escalation, and the reason-code-change event can read this tick's caps without recomputing them, and they are surfaced on the controller status payload for display (as `clearance_ahead_cm`, `atc_speed_limit`, `current_block_speed_limit`, and `speed_limit_reason`). They are per-tick display caches of the lookahead computation, not independently-written live control fields, so the distance-0 **canonical lookahead payload** stays the single source of truth for target speed and reason code and the **Controller retained field schema** rule does not require them to appear in its table. See **Lookahead is a pure derived value**, **canonical lookahead payload**, **ATC speed limit**, and **Speed curves** below.
- **ATO Computer** — handle-selection / curve-tracking / braking-notch logic, `ato.running` lifecycle, and depart-in-ATO acceptance. Lives in `train_controller/ato.py` (class `ATOComputer`); accessed externally as `controller.ato.running` (run-active flag), `controller.ato.info` (destination snapshot), `controller.ato.debug` (per-tick debug payload), `controller.ato.go()` / `controller.ato.stop()` (run lifecycle), `controller.ato.compute_handle(delta_seconds)` (per-tick handle selection), `controller.ato.compute_info()`, `controller.ato.sample_curve_at(curve, distance_cm, key)`, `controller.ato.simulate_forward(speed, handle, distance_cm, dt)`, `controller.ato.calculate_power_notch(...)`, and `controller.ato.calculate_braking_notch_for_speed(...)`. The module-level `rate_limit_handle(...)` helper lives in the same file. See **`ato.running` meaning and lifecycle** and **ATO handle calculation** below.
- **EB Workflow** — `eb.active`, EB activation effects, release contract, dwell exception. Lives in `train_controller/eb.py`; accessed as `controller.eb.active` (latch), `controller.eb.activate()` (operator-issued EB), `controller.eb.release()` (the gated operator clear), and `controller.eb.clear()` (the EB-owned ungated clear used only by `TrainController.complete_power_off()` during OFF cleanup — it sets `eb.active = False` with no gate, distinct from the precondition-gated `eb.release()`). These three methods are the only sites that assign `eb.active`; the full single-writer rule is Module boundaries rule 2 below. The canonical home is the **EB workflow state machine** table below in this section; controller-side tick handling appears in **Controller tick order** below.
- **Manual driving** — `simulation` and `power_percent` submode behavior; `manual.manual_power_percent`. Writes the `simulation`-submode notch through the Operational-state sub-module per Module boundaries rule 5. Lives in `train_controller/manual.py` (class `ManualDriving`); accessed externally as `controller.manual.manual_mode_type` and `controller.manual.manual_power_percent`. The operator-facing setters `set_manual_mode_type(...)` / `set_manual_power_percent(...)` live on the operator command surface and write through to these fields. See **Manual mode and movement-authority boundary** below.

*Output layer — what the computer writes:*

- **Notification emission** — the controller's adapter onto the one runtime event stream. Lives in `train_controller/notifications.py` (class `Notifications`, accessed as `controller.notifications`). It holds no queue and no state. `controller.notifications.emit(operation, kind, message, error=None, payload=None, latch_event=False)` fills in `source = "TrainController"` and an `entities` list naming this train, then forwards every argument, including `latch_event`, to `NotificationCenter.emit(...)` per the **Event schema**; the caller passes its own function name as `operation`. Every controller-side report — each drained command's result, each acceptance/transition command's result (`depart()`, `enter_station_dwell()`, `finish_dwell()`), EB activation and release, latch writes through the **Writer-helper rule**, and the ATC reason-code change of **Controller tick order** substep `4d7c` — goes through this one adapter. Each of those emits on both outcomes: `kind = "info"` on acceptance and `"warning"` on rejection, with `{success, reason}` in `payload`. Those acceptance events are what the **Event log** records as "departed" and "entered station dwell". The frontend reads them back through `GET /api/trains/<train_id>/notifications`, which is a filter over the stream per **Runtime notifications** and empties nothing.

The Action latches owned by `TrainController` live nested under `TrainController.route_hooks.phase_latches: PhaseLatches` (its seven transition and teardown fields, named under the **Controller retained field schema** and the **Latch Table**) and are documented in the **Latch Table** in the Core Runtime Loop section. `TrainController` owns the in-memory storage; the Latch Table is the single canonical home for writers, helpers, consumers, gating predicates, and lifecycle.

**Module boundaries.** These rules consolidate the "only X writes Y" constraints that apply across the chapter:

1. The Operational state machine is the only writer of `state`.
2. The EB Workflow is the only writer of `eb.active`: `eb.activate()` sets it `True`, and `eb.release()` / `eb.clear()` set it `False`. The ATC overspeed and no-authority escalation inside `TrainController.tick(...)` raises EB by calling `controller.eb.activate()`, so it applies the **canonical EB activation effects** through that one routine instead of assigning the field. The activate gate (`eb.active == False`) can never reject that call, because tick-order step `d483` early-exits the tick whenever EB is already latched, before the ATC overspeed step `914f` runs. The Action OFF cleanup clears the flag through the EB-owned `controller.eb.clear()` helper rather than assigning the field itself. No runtime site outside `train_controller/eb.py` assigns `eb.active`. The one sanctioned direct assignment is state restore: `TrainController` deserialization (in `train_controller/serialization.py`) rebuilds the saved latch by assigning `controller.eb.active` from the snapshot, which replays stored state rather than running EB logic, so the three `eb.py` methods stay the only runtime writers.
3. The ATC Computer is the only computation site for `lookahead`.
4. Action latches are written only through the writer-helpers listed in the **Latch Table** preamble; no sub-module assigns latch fields directly.
5. **`handle_position` single writer.** `handle_position` is written only through the Operational-state sub-module.
   - **Three command producers.** Three sites produce a driver/ATO command: manual `simulation`; ATO (`ATOComputer.compute_handle(...)` while running, or `ATOComputer.calculate_braking_notch_for_speed(...)` against the live distance-0 `atc_limit` while not — see tick step `8d18`); and the EB Workflow.
   - **Three override writers, in precedence order.** Three override writers may replace that tick's command afterward, in tick order `b41e` → `b7ac` → `c2fe`, all routed through the same sub-module. Each later writer in that order outranks the ones before it, with one exception:
     - tick step `b41e`'s call to `OperationalStateMachine.set_service_brake_to_zero()` — service-stop override, lowest precedence
     - tick step `b7ac`'s re-application of the EB Workflow's own `handle_position = EB` write — highest precedence
     - tick step `c2fe`'s neutral-notch write, gated on `eb.active == False` so it can never override `b7ac`'s EB write despite running after it — the one precedence exception the tick order alone does not express

     So the effective precedence is EB > pending-power-off propulsion hold > service-stop override.
   - **`manual.manual_power_percent` stays separate.** It stays encapsulated by Manual driving and its `ManualDriving.reset_power_percent_for_safety()` helper, outside this precedence chain.
   - **Two reset helpers, no overlap.** All non-driving resets use one of two distinct Operational-state helpers:
     - `OperationalStateMachine.reset_handle_to_neutral()` writes the neutral notch. It is called by `TrainController._apply_power_off_request()`, `TrainController.commands.set_manual_mode_type()` when entering `power_percent`, `TrainController.complete_power_off()`, and tick step `c2fe` on every tick `phase_latches.power_off` remains set and `eb.active` is `False`.
     - `OperationalStateMachine.set_service_brake_to_zero()` writes the ordinary service-brake-to-zero notch. It is called only by tick step `b41e`.

     Tick step `d483` re-applies the EB Workflow's own `handle_position = EB` write on every tick EB stays latched from a prior tick; tick step `b7ac` covers the escalation tick itself, before `d483` runs on a later tick. No helper is permitted to produce both reset values, and no other writer exists.
6. The Operator command surface is the only entry point for external operator commands. An external EB activate/release request belongs to that surface: it enqueues a command that the drain runs at slots 6 and 7 of the canonical drain order, and the drain slot is what calls `controller.eb.activate()` / `controller.eb.release()`. Those two methods themselves execute synchronously and evaluate their own gates at the moment they are called, whether that call comes from the drain slot or, for `eb.activate()`, from ATC overspeed escalation calling it directly inside `TrainController.tick()` (see the **canonical EB activation effects**) — `eb.activate()` / `eb.release()` do not themselves enqueue anything. Apart from the operator command surface and that one ATC escalation call, no external caller invokes ATC, ATO, EB, or manual driving sub-modules directly.

**Data flow per tick.**

- *Input:* the Operator command surface drains queued commands at the start of `TrainController.tick(...)`; the Path plan projection refreshes on every read of `received_path_plan`; Physics sync absorbs `PhysicsSpanUpdate` from `TrainPhysics.tick(...)`; Route hooks fire when `RouteExecutor` or `PathDispatcher` calls them.
- *Compute:* the Operational state machine evaluates reactive transitions in Observe (inside `TrainController.on_physics_updated(...)`), while the ATC Computer computes `lookahead` and the ATO Computer (in ATO mode) or Manual driving (in manual mode) produces the active command in Action (inside `TrainController.tick(...)`); the EB Workflow can override the result at any step, and tick step `b41e` replaces it with service braking when `ops.service_stop_active` is set.
- *Output:* Notification emission flows to `NotificationCenter`; Action latches are written when accepted commands or in-tick escalations need deferred dispatcher cancellation; controller-state writes land on the canonical retained fields.

**Controller state**

- `TrainController` owns live power/cab state: `state` (canonical operational state, including `OFF`), active cab selection, and the live direction selection implied by that cab. The convenience read `power_on` is derived from `state != "OFF"`; it has no separate writer. These are not re-synced from `Train` on every tick.
- `TrainController` owns the train's live physical span and speed. `TrainPhysics.tick(...)` computes movement and emits `PhysicsSpanUpdate`; `TrainController.on_physics_updated(...)` is the normal writer that applies the new span/speed to controller-owned storage. `Train` itself does not store live position/span.
- `manual.manual_mode_type` holds the manual submode: `simulation` or `power_percent`.
- `TrainController.travel_direction` is a **read-only derived value**, computed each time it is read from `(self.cab, self.current_span)`. There is no stored field and there are no writers. The mapping rule works like this. The cab's physical end (`end_a` or `end_b` per `TrainSpan`) is the head. `travel_direction` is the network-frame direction that points from the opposite physical end, through the cab end, and onward into the next span resource ahead. When there is no next span resource ahead of the cab end (for example, the cab end is at a track-end, dead-end, or disabled-resource boundary, or the consist sits on a single tile with no live forward connectivity), `travel_direction` is the network-frame direction outward through the cab edge of the cab end's tile. This rule depends only on consist-and-cab geometry, not on `received_path_plan`. When `self.cab is None`, the value is `None`. A successful write to `cab` (any of the three cab writers — `TrainController.commands.set_cab(...)`, the ATO cab alignment inside `TrainController.depart()`, or `TrainController.commands.clear_cab()` — per **Allowed `(state, cab)` pairs**) writes only `cab`. It does not "atomically update" `travel_direction`, because there is no field to update; the next read of `travel_direction` recomputes from the new cab.
- `manual.manual_power_percent` is the `power_percent`-mode manual control input: an integer `0..100` voltage-style command rather than a signed traction/brake command.
- `phase_latches.power_off: bool` is the stopped-only shutdown latch — row `f8d5` in the **Latch Table**, which owns its writer, consumer, and gating rules. It is the canonical handoff that moves power-off from command acceptance into the standard per-train stage workflow.
- `TrainController` owns the per-train Action retained latch / flag aggregate in v1. The aggregate is `phase_latches: PhaseLatches`, with seven fields: `departure_request`, `station_entry_request`, `station_exit_request`, `path_cancel_request`, `route_abort`, `power_off`, and `route_deactivate`. `ControllerProgressReport` values are not retained controller fields. Observe appends them to the controller-owned per-train progress mailbox (`physics_sync.queued_progress_reports`): the final `on_physics_updated(...)` callback for a train whose movement is calculated, or `TrainController.build_detected_progress_report()` for a train whose movement is not calculated (per **Movement feedback runs only when movement is calculated; detection feedback always runs**), and that same Observe pass drains and clears the mailbox before Plan begins either way. The retained-field schema below lists `phase_latches` as a single field; the seven nested fields are documented inside the **Latch Table**. Dwell entry is latch-based: Plan step `3a37` in `RouteExecutor.tick_train_plan(...)` writes the dwell start timestamps and `station_entry_request`; the Action station-entry consumer calls `TrainController.enter_station_dwell()`.
- **Entering `READY`.** A controller enters `READY` from `OFF` when power is turned on, per the **`READY` state** definition. Selecting or deselecting a cab while stopped keeps the controller in `READY`.
- **Route authority without a selected cab.** Route authority may still be assigned while a cab is unselected, and `RouteExecutor` must not treat a missing cab as a blocker for `create_path(...)`. `TrainController.depart()` accepts authority per its canonical contract; auto-cab selection on success is part of that contract and is not restated here.
- **Pre-depart manual movement.** Manual input may move the train even before `depart()` is accepted (controller still in `READY`), but only when `received_path_plan is not None`, so the canonical lookahead in step `22a9` exposes a path-bound ATC limit at distance 0. Without a live path, the no-authority empty payload sets `atc_limit = 0` at distance 0, and ATC holds the train at rest until a route assigns authority. Pre-depart manual movement cannot satisfy path stop-completion until `controller.state == RUNNING_MOVING`. That state is reached by either of these two equally valid transitions:
  - a successful `TrainController.depart()` acceptance
  - the reactive `READY → RUNNING_MOVING` transition performed by `OperationalStateMachine.evaluate_reactive_conditions()` after `TrainController.on_physics_updated(...)` writes a new speed (see **Reactive condition evaluation** and the `RUNNING_MOVING` state row)

  Such pre-depart manual movement may still produce head-entry route progress, such as `task_kind == "waypoint"` consumption; only stop-completion is gated on `state == RUNNING_MOVING`.
- Manual driving is `control_mode == manual`; there is no separate `MANUAL` operational state.
- `assigned_path_id: Optional[str]` is a computed read-only property derived from `received_path_plan.path_id`; it is the controller-facing runtime read and is not stored or written independently.
- `received_path_plan` is the controller's read-only live movement-authority projection over the active dispatcher-owned path.
- `received_path_plan` is not stored controller state and has no writer. `PathDispatcher` owns the underlying `Path`; `TrainController` reads the projection and must not mutate path ownership or lifecycle.
- `TrainController` is also the canonical query and storage home for the train's current occupied span. The live span is produced by `TrainPhysics` and written into `TrainController.physics_sync.current_span`. Block and switch resources still carry their own physical `occupied_by` ownership, but tile-level ends and ordered occupied tiles live on the controller span, not on `Train`. `RouteExecutor` and `PathDispatcher` ask the controller for one cab-independent physical span read, instead of deriving it on their own from `Train`. That span read must expose the ordered occupied span in physical order (`occupied_blocks` and `occupied_tiles`), plus the two explicit physical end locators needed for later ordering comparisons. The occupancy list is the block-level ownership view; the end locators are the tile-level precise geometry view. The read does not depend on a currently selected cab.

**Controller retained field schema**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | controller state enum | Canonical operational state (`OFF`, `READY`, `RUNNING_MOVING`, `RUNNING_AT_STATION`). Stored on the Operational state machine sub-module and accessed externally as `controller.ops.state`; the bare `controller.state` spelling used elsewhere is shorthand for it. |
| `power_on` | `bool` (read-only derived: `state != "OFF"`) | Convenience read for "is the controller powered on?" Computed each access from `state`; not a stored field; no writers. Power transitions are owned by the canonical `state` machine, not by a parallel boolean. |
| `commands.cab` | `Optional[str]` | Active cab selection (`"A"`, `"B"`, or `None`). Stored on the `OperatorCommands` sub-module; serialized under the key `"cab"`. |
| `commands.control_mode` | `"ato" \| "manual"` | High-level driving mode selector. Stored on the `OperatorCommands` sub-module; serialized under the key `"control_mode"`. |
| `manual.manual_mode_type` | `"simulation" \| "power_percent"` | Manual-mode submode selector. Construction default is `simulation`. Mutated only through `TrainController.commands.set_manual_mode_type(...)`. |
| `travel_direction` | `Optional[str]` (read-only property) | Read-only derived value computed each read from `(self.cab, self.current_span)`. Not a stored field; no writers. See the `travel_direction` derivation rule above. |
| `ops.handle_position` | controller handle enum/value | Active handle command for ATO and manual `simulation` mode |
| `manual.manual_power_percent` | `int` | Active manual driver command for manual `power_percent` mode (`0..100`) |
| `eb.active` | `bool` | Emergency-brake latch |
| `ato.running` | `bool` | Whether an ATO run is presently active (the train has been commanded to run under ATO and has not yet been halted, dwelled, EB'd, or otherwise stopped). This is a run-active flag, not a mode flag; the mode flag is `control_mode`. |
| `ops.service_stop_active` | `bool` | Latch that arms service braking for Plan timed-`run` completion; the **Latch Table** is its canonical home and defines the writer, the consumer, and the gating state. Default `False`. While it is set, Controller tick step `b41e` replaces that tick's ATO/manual propulsion command with service stopping. |
| `phase_latches` | `PhaseLatches` | Aggregate of the seven Action latches the controller owns: the three transition requests `departure_request: bool`, `station_entry_request: bool`, `station_exit_request: bool`, plus `path_cancel_request: Optional[PendingPathCancelRequest]`, `route_abort: bool`, `power_off: bool`, `route_deactivate: bool`. Writers go through `controller.route_hooks.phase_latches.set_*(...)`; each field's own named Action consumer step clears it as part of performing its transition or teardown call (there is no separate `consume_*()` accessor on `PhaseLatches`; see the **Naming convention** paragraph in the Core Runtime Loop section). The full lifecycle for each field — gating predicates, multi-tick survival, fan-out — lives in the **Latch Table** in the Core Runtime Loop section. |
| `received_path_plan` | `Optional[ReceivedPathPlan]` (read-only property) | Live read of the controller's active movement authority. Computed each time through the controller's injected active-path projection reader, which delegates to `PathDispatcher.get_active_path(train_id)` and returns the canonical **received_path_plan schema**. Not a stored field; there is no `TrainController.receive_path_plan(...)` setter. The projection exposes only controller-needed authority fields such as `path_id`, `resource_sequence`, and `authority_end_block_id`; only `Path.status` lifecycle state stays dispatcher-owned, and the requested target lives route-side on `RouteRun.task_runs[i].resolved_target`. `None` when the train has no `ACTIVE` path. |
| `physics_sync.current_span` | `TrainSpan` | Controller-owned live physical span, including ordered occupied resources/blocks/tiles and both physical end locators. Lives on the `PhysicsSync` sub-module. |
| `physics_sync.current_speed_kmh` | `float` | Controller-owned live physical speed normally written by `TrainController.on_physics_updated(...)` from the `PhysicsSpanUpdate` produced by `TrainPhysics.tick(...)`. `TrainController.complete_power_off()` writes no speed — a normally-stopped power-off is already at `0`, and `SimulationController.clear_failed_runtime()` sets the speed to `0` directly for a still-rolling ghost train it halts. Lives on the `PhysicsSync` sub-module. |
| `physics_sync.pending_detected_entered_blocks` / `pending_detected_vacated_blocks` | `Set[str]` each | Named within-tick Observe → Observe handoff (Observe writes them, and the same Observe pass folds them into the occupancy commit). Observe resets both to empty for every train, then writes this tick's attributed block IDs onto each affected train; `pending_detected_vacated_blocks` carries only the clears the holding train's calculated tail has reached the exit seam of; every other confirmed clear is held and re-offered on a later read (see **Power**, A clear read from under the train is a detection fault). The final `on_physics_updated(...)` callback folds them into that tick's block observations and clears both immediately for a train whose movement is calculated; `TrainController.build_detected_progress_report()` does the same for a train whose movement is not calculated (per **Movement feedback runs only when movement is calculated; detection feedback always runs**). Neither survives the train transaction and neither is a latch. |
| `physics_sync.pending_block_exit_edges` | `Dict[str, edge]` | Per-block held tail-vacate direction: when the calculated tail leaves a block, `TrainController.on_physics_updated(...)` records that block's forward `exit_edge` here and consumes the entry when the debounced detector vacate fires (per **Power**, Block occupancy detection), so `BlockManager.on_block_tail_vacated(...)` receives the same caution `direction` despite the detector lag. Observe writes the same field for an unidentified train, whose edge comes from its detected blocks and is consumed on that same tick (see **Power**, Unidentified trains). The one `PhysicsSync` buffer that may hold an entry across ticks. |
| `presence_unknown` | `bool` | The last Observe detector pass's verdict on whether this train's calculated position still has physical detection behind it. Observe's presence-unknown step computes the verdict from the train's evidence set — its span's `occupied_blocks` plus the blocks it holds through `Block.occupied_by`, intersected with `OccupancyInput.detected_block_ids()`, `True` when that intersection is empty (no detection anywhere in the evidence set), per **Power**, Ghosted trains — and writes it here every detector pass; it is not recomputed on arbitrary reads. It is not a latch: because Observe overwrites it every pass, detection returning anywhere in the evidence set clears it on the next pass. Observe also reads the stored value before overwriting it, so this one field doubles as the rising-edge memory — the ghost teardown fires when the freshly computed verdict is `True` and the stored value was `False` — and there is no separate previous-value field. Default `False`. Serialized on the controller payload. |
| `_last_emitted_atc_reason_code` | `Optional[str]` | Last distance-0 `atc_limit_reason_code` this controller emitted a change event for. Written by tick substep `4d7c` immediately after that substep emits, and reset to `None` at tick substep `3ec8` when the train is powered off — an off train computes no limit, so whatever code it powers back on with is reported as a change even if it matches the code it went down with. No other command or state transition resets it. Lives on the `TrainController` controller façade. |
| `_overspeed_warned` | `bool` | Whether tick substep `914f` has already emitted the below-EB-margin overspeed warning for the current continuous over-margin occurrence. Written only by substep `914f`: set `True` immediately after it emits, and cleared once `current_speed_kmh` no longer exceeds `atc_limit_at_distance_0 + OVERSPEED_WARN_THRESHOLD_KMH`, so the warning re-emits on the next fresh occurrence. Default `False`. Lives on the `TrainController` controller façade. |
| `lookahead` | canonical lookahead payload (read-only property) | Computed from `(current_span, cab, received_path_plan, network_state, signals, current_speed_kmh, eb.active)`. Pure derived value; not a stored field; no persistent or cross-tick cache. A within-tick memo is allowed only under the invalidation, disposal, and shadow-check rules in **Lookahead is a pure derived value**. See **canonical lookahead payload** below for the schema returned by each read. |
| `ato.info` | ATO destination snapshot | Written on every tick that reaches tick step `0a4e` (`ATOComputer.compute_info()`), overwriting the prior tick's value; the last value is retained across a tick that early-exits before `0a4e` (no train / `OFF` at `3ec8`, or EB latched at `d483`). Diagnostic/UI-facing only: no runtime control decision reads it. |
| `ato.debug` | per-tick ATO debug payload | Written on every tick that reaches tick step `0a4e`, alongside `ato.info`, overwriting the prior tick's value; the last value is retained across a tick that early-exits before `0a4e`. Diagnostic/UI-facing only: no runtime control decision reads it. |

- The table above is the canonical retained controller field set for v1. If a field is not in this table or in a later canonical payload schema, it must not remain as an independently written live controller field.

- **`ControllerCondition` set** (canonical home; referenced elsewhere by name). `ControllerCondition` is the canonical enum of currently-active controller-state conditions used to express recovery and create-eligibility predicates. v1 values:

  - `HAS_AUTHORITY` — `received_path_plan is not None`
  - `EB_LATCHED` — `eb.active == True`
  - `POWER_OFF_PENDING` — `controller.route_hooks.phase_latches.power_off == True`
  - `PATH_CANCEL_PENDING` — `controller.route_hooks.phase_latches.path_cancel_request is not None`
  - `ROUTE_ABORT_PENDING` — `controller.route_hooks.phase_latches.route_abort == True`
  - `ROUTE_DEACTIVATE_PENDING` — `controller.route_hooks.phase_latches.route_deactivate == True`

  `TrainController.active_conditions` is a derived `FrozenSet[ControllerCondition]` computed each read from the controller's stored fields per the mapping above. Not a stored field; no writers.

  `TrainController.is_recovery_clean` (derived `bool`): `state == READY` AND `active_conditions` contains none of `{HAS_AUTHORITY, EB_LATCHED, POWER_OFF_PENDING}`. This is the canonical "controller has reached the stopped recovery state" predicate. Other sites cross-reference it by name and must not restate the conjuncts.

  `RouteExecutor.is_clean_for_create(train_id)` (derived `bool`): `controller.is_recovery_clean` AND `active_conditions` contains none of `{PATH_CANCEL_PENDING, ROUTE_ABORT_PENDING, ROUTE_DEACTIVATE_PENDING}` AND `run.path_cancelled is False`. This is the canonical "Plan may run the create branch" predicate.

  Adding a new latch in a future revision requires all three edits in the same patch: add its `ControllerCondition` value, add the mapping used by `TrainController.active_conditions`, and update every predicate's explicit excluded set when that latch must block the predicate. The current predicates do not automatically include a new enum member.

- **Allowed `(state, cab)` pairs.** The relationship between `state` and `cab` is structurally constrained but enforced by its three cab writers — `TrainController.commands.set_cab(...)`, the ATO cab selection inside `TrainController.depart()`, and `TrainController.commands.clear_cab()` during OFF cleanup — plus the cab precondition on `TrainController.enter_station_dwell()`. The legal combinations are:

  | `state` | `cab` |
  | --- | --- |
  | `OFF` | `None` |
  | `READY` | `None` or `"A"` or `"B"` |
  | `RUNNING_MOVING` | `"A"` or `"B"` |
  | `RUNNING_AT_STATION` | `"A"` or `"B"` |

  Any other combination is a contract violation. Readers needing cab membership read `cab` directly; the state alone does not encode it.

**Lookahead is a pure derived value**

`TrainController.get_lookahead()` returns the canonical lookahead payload (the `Dict` shape defined in **canonical lookahead payload**). `TrainController.lookahead` is the per-block `LookaheadPoint` list projection over the same computation. Both are computed each time they are read, from `(current_span, cab, received_path_plan, network_state, signals, current_speed_kmh, eb.active)`. `received_path_plan` supplies the ordered authorized corridor. Speed limits, block/switch state, signal-derived diagnostics, and physical position are resolved from the live network/controller state, not copied into the controller authority payload. There is no stored authority-payload field, and no separate "pre-physics" / "post-physics" copies; every read returns the live result. A within-tick memo may cache the computed result across reads inside a single tick, as an implementation optimization, as long as it is discarded before the next tick, is invalidated by a write to any of this computation's own inputs — `current_span`, `cab`, `received_path_plan`, `network_state`, `signals`, `current_speed_kmh`, or `eb.active` — including the just-updated span/speed a same-tick `TrainController.on_physics_updated(...)` call writes, and is shadow-verified identical to a live recompute, so every caller still sees the live result. Persistent / cross-tick projection caching with an invalidation surface stays Out of Scope; see the **Out of Scope** section.

**Controller state machine**

**`READY` state** (referenced elsewhere by name): the controller's `READY` state means powered, stopped, not dwelling, regardless of cab selection. Other sites must cross-reference `state == READY` and must not invent additional substate names for it.

| State | Meaning | Canonical entry triggers | Canonical exits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `OFF` (`414b`) | Power off. `TrainController.eb.activate()` is accepted while `OFF` (see **EB workflow state machine**, `eb.active` while `OFF`). | Action power-off cleanup consuming `TrainController.pending_power_off` — from the stopped Action operator writer, or from the Observe ghosted-train writer once its inclusive cancel has committed (**Power**, Ghosted trains); `SimulationController.clear_failed_runtime()` (step `7c41`); startup default. Every entry except the startup default reaches `OFF` through `TrainController.complete_power_off()`. | `TrainController.commands.power_on_cmd()`, `set_mode(...)`, or `set_cab(...)` while in manual mode (any of these power `OFF → READY`; `power_on_cmd()` carries any latched `eb.active` into `READY` without clearing it) |
| `READY` (`601a`) | Powered, stopped, not dwelling. Cab may or may not be selected. | `TrainController.commands.power_on_cmd()`; `TrainController.commands.set_mode(...)` while stopped — from `OFF` as a power-up side effect, and from stopped `RUNNING_MOVING`; `TrainController.commands.set_cab(...)` while stopped (manual mode only, including the `OFF`-power-up variant); `OperationalStateMachine.evaluate_reactive_conditions()` applying the stopped/no-authority rule after authority release, cancellation, revocation, or EB release; `TrainController.finish_dwell()`. The evaluator runs after a physics update and again after the Action command drain and its early-Action consumers (step `71ee`), so it does not depend on movement calculation having run this tick. A driver in manual mode who voluntarily stops under positive clearance with live authority remains in `RUNNING_MOVING` per the next row. See **Reactive condition evaluation** below for the full predicate set. | `TrainController.depart()` → `RUNNING_MOVING`; `OperationalStateMachine.evaluate_reactive_conditions()` when a cab is selected and `not TrainController.is_stopped()` (see below); `TrainController.enter_station_dwell()` after its cab precondition; `TrainController.commands.power_off_cmd()` → writes `pending_power_off` (no synchronous exit); the Action power-off cleanup consumer performs the `READY → OFF` transition |
| `RUNNING_MOVING` (`185a`) | Depart accepted for the current authority. The train may be physically moving, or stopped at zero ATC clearance under the same live authority while waiting for clearance / authority extension. `RUNNING_MOVING` is the canonical "depart-accepted" indicator used by stop-completion eligibility and other readers. | `TrainController.depart()` acceptance (which guarantees a cab aligned to the authority, selecting or switching it if needed); `OperationalStateMachine.evaluate_reactive_conditions()` when the controller observes a selected cab and `not TrainController.is_stopped()` while in `READY` (rare manual edge case: a driver pre-rolls before depart was issued; once depart is accepted the controller transitions). | `READY` through `OperationalStateMachine.evaluate_reactive_conditions()` when the train is stopped, has no live authority, and `eb.active == False`; stopped-only operator commands accepted while `is_stopped()` is true: `set_cab(...)` (manual mode only) → `READY`, `set_mode(...)` → `READY`, `power_off_cmd()` → writes `pending_power_off`, with Action power-off cleanup exiting through `READY` to `OFF`. An operator ATO-stop — the stop button, not EB — ends the ATO run by clearing `ato.running` through `TrainController.ato.stop()`; the controller then brakes the train and, once it is stopped, the tick's ATO command step moves it to `READY` even while live authority is still held. `READY` here means only that the train is stopped and free to depart with nothing (no EB, no ended run) blocking a fresh start; it does not mean the train has released its authority, and a later `TrainController.depart()` resumes the run against that same held authority. This is an explicit operator exit, distinct from the automatic no-authority reactive exit above. There is no direct `RUNNING_MOVING → RUNNING_AT_STATION` edge: confirmed arrival first lands in `READY`; the Plan dwell-entry step then writes `station_entry_request`, and the Action station-entry consumer's `TrainController.enter_station_dwell()` call performs `READY → RUNNING_AT_STATION`. |
| `RUNNING_AT_STATION` (`90c4`) | Route-managed dwell at a confirmed stop task | Plan's `RouteExecutor.tick_train_plan(...)` dwell-entry step writes `station_entry_request` when the next non-finished task on the directed walk has `task_kind == "dwell"`; the Action station-entry consumer calls `TrainController.enter_station_dwell()`. The controller does not detect dwell entry on its own; it never reads `RouteRun`. | `TrainController.finish_dwell()` (the Action station-exit consumer of `station_exit_request`, written by the Plan dwell-complete step) → `READY`. Changes to controller conditions, including EB activation or release, do not themselves write this route-owned operational state; while EB is active the general Plan eligibility rule prevents dwell completion and departure. `TrainController.commands.set_cab(...)` (manual mode only) and `TrainController.commands.set_mode(...)` apply their side effects but preserve `RUNNING_AT_STATION`. Any of the three Action teardown consumers (`pending_route_abort`, `pending_power_off`, `pending_route_deactivate`) calls `RouteExecutor.remove_train_route_run(...)`, which writes `station_exit_request`; the later Action station-exit consumer performs the exit. |

- **Reactive condition evaluation**: `OperationalStateMachine.evaluate_reactive_conditions()` is the one implementation of the two automatic transitions below. `TrainController.on_physics_updated(span_update)` calls it synchronously after writing speed and before building the progress report. `TrainController.tick(...)` calls it again after the command drain and early dispatcher callback, so it sees both command changes and any authority cancellation that just committed. Both calls are idempotent and use `TrainController.is_stopped()`.
  - If `state == READY`, `cab ∈ {"A", "B"}`, and `not TrainController.is_stopped()`: transition to `RUNNING_MOVING`. The cab guard is mandatory because every legal `RUNNING_MOVING` pair has a selected cab; motion observed from cabless `READY` is an invariant violation and must not be normalized into an illegal state. This is one of the two canonical state-machine transitions into `RUNNING_MOVING` (the other is a successful `TrainController.depart()` call); both are equally legitimate first-class transitions. After this transition, call `TrainController.ato.go()` unconditionally — the canonical helper that verifies its own preconditions and sets `ato.running = True` per the **`ato.running` meaning and lifecycle** section. This rule covers several cases: a manual driver pre-rolls under live authority before Plan's `depart()` lands; ATC clearance returns under live authority and physics resumes motion before the next Plan tick; and any other path that legitimately produces motion from cab-selected `READY`.
  - If `state == RUNNING_MOVING` and `TrainController.is_stopped()` and the train has no live authority and `TrainController.eb.active == False`: transition to `READY`. This is the no-authority braking-completion path. While live authority still exists and the train is stopped, the controller stays in `RUNNING_MOVING`; clearance may return and movement may resume without a fresh `depart()` call. While EB is latched (`eb.active == True`) the evaluator does not fire. `TrainController.eb.release()` only clears that condition; the post-command call to this same evaluator performs the state transition when the remaining ordinary predicates hold. `RUNNING_AT_STATION` is not one of this rule's source states and is therefore preserved.
  - While live authority still exists, `TrainController.is_stopped() == True` alone never causes the reactive exit from `RUNNING_MOVING` — whether the stop is voluntary (the driver stopped under positive clearance) or ATC-forced (zero clearance, for example a best-effort truncated authority whose `authority_end_block_id` is short of the armed stop target after `PathDispatcher.extend_path(...)` appended nothing; see tick step `90d3`). In both cases clearance may return when the path extends or conditions change, and motion resumes without a fresh `TrainController.depart()` call. The no-authority case above is the only automatic stopped exit. Explicit operator commands are separate exits and are not bound by that no-authority condition: accepted `TrainController.commands.set_cab(...)` or `TrainController.commands.set_mode(...)` moves to `READY`, an operator ATO-stop (the stop button, which clears `ato.running` through `TrainController.ato.stop()`) moves the train to `READY` once it has braked to a stop even while it still holds live authority, and `TrainController.commands.power_off_cmd()` begins the later `OFF` teardown. An operator stop landing in `READY` under held authority is intended: `READY` is the not-in-emergency, free-to-depart state, not a claim that authority was released, and the held authority lets a later `depart()` resume the run.
- The state machine above is the single canonical operational-state contract. Shared logic must not introduce additional live route/runtime state enums for path completion or cancellation recovery in v1.
- **`RUNNING_AT_STATION` invariant**: `received_path_plan is None` whenever `state == RUNNING_AT_STATION`. Authority release (`PathDispatcher.try_complete_active_path(...)`) transitions the `Path` to `COMPLETED` in Observe; only after that transition does Plan's dwell-entry step (`3a37`) fire and write `station_entry_request`, whose Action consumer calls `TrainController.enter_station_dwell()`. No code path may call `TrainController.enter_station_dwell()` while a `Path` with `status == ACTIVE` still exists for this train. Consequently any general workflow that requests cancellation only when live authority exists naturally writes no cancellation latch during dwell.
- Stopped-only operator commands (`power_off_cmd()`, `set_cab(...)` in manual mode, and `set_mode(...)`) may be issued from any physically stopped controller state, including `OFF`. `set_mode(...)` (any mode), and `set_cab(...)` (manual mode only), issued while `OFF` also power the controller up as a side effect: they land it in `READY` (the same `OFF → READY` transition `power_on_cmd()` performs; see the `OFF` state-table row) while also applying the cab/mode change, because selecting a cab or mode is a way of bringing a stopped train under control. `power_off_cmd()` while `OFF` is accepted as a no-op (the train is already off). In v1 these commands disengage any active ATO run and land in `READY` (or `OFF` after pending power-off cleanup). They do not cause automatic movement just because clearance later returns or dwell later finishes.
- Stopped recovery commands transition to `READY` (regardless of cab); powered off remains `OFF`.

**`ato.running` meaning and lifecycle**

- `ato.running` means "an ATO run is currently in progress": the train has been commanded to move under ATO via `TrainController.depart()` / `TrainController.ato.go()`, and that run has not yet ended through arrival-at-dwell, path completion, authority clear, EB, or any stopped-state command (power / cab / mode). `TrainController.ato.go()` itself verifies `control_mode == "ato"` and `received_path_plan is not None` before it sets `ato.running = True`, and no-ops otherwise; both of its ATO-mode callers invoke it unconditionally on their own triggering transition, so neither caller duplicates that precondition check. It is a **run-active** flag, not a **mode** flag. The mode flag is `control_mode` (`ato` vs `manual`), which says what kind of driving the controller is set up for. `ato.running` says whether an ATO run is currently driving the train. A train in ATO mode is not always `ato.running`: before the first `depart()`, between runs, during dwell, and after any run-ending event, `control_mode == ato` but `ato.running == False`. When the train is stopped with zero ATC clearance but the same live authority still exists (that is, still in `RUNNING_MOVING` with `is_stopped() == True`), the run has not ended; `ato.running` stays `True` so the controller auto-resumes when clearance returns. A train in manual mode is never `ato.running`.
- `ato.running = True` is set by the canonical state-machine transition into `RUNNING_MOVING`, whenever `control_mode == "ato"` and `received_path_plan is not None` at the moment of transition. This applies to both ATO-mode transition triggers: a successful `TrainController.depart()` acceptance in `ato` mode (which calls `TrainController.ato.go()`), and `OperationalStateMachine.evaluate_reactive_conditions()` entering `RUNNING_MOVING` from `READY` while already in `ato` mode. Both transitions converge on the same `ato.running` write. `TrainController.ato.go()` is the canonical helper that verifies the precondition and performs the `ato.running` write; both transition sites call it unconditionally for `ato.running` — including the evaluator firing in manual mode, where `TrainController.ato.go()`'s own precondition check makes the call a no-op. The `state` move into `RUNNING_MOVING` is a separate write: the evaluator calls `OperationalStateMachine.enter_running_moving()` itself in both modes (before its unconditional `TrainController.ato.go()` call, per **Reactive condition evaluation**), while `TrainController.depart()` moves `state` through `TrainController.ato.go()` in `ato` mode and by calling `OperationalStateMachine.enter_running_moving()` directly in `manual` mode. No other command, tick handler, or callback flips `ato.running` to `True`. In particular, `TrainController.commands.set_cab(...)`, `TrainController.commands.set_mode(...)`, `TrainController.eb.release()`, `TrainController.enter_station_dwell()`, and `TrainController.finish_dwell()` never set `ato.running = True`.
- `ato.running` has exactly one writer: `TrainController`. Neither `RouteExecutor` nor `PathDispatcher` nor any train-side mirror writes this flag directly; train-running state is not a route executor's concern. `controller.ato.stop()` is the canonical helper that clears `ato.running`; it is idempotent, and every canonical run-ending event calls it rather than assigning the field: authority clear (tick substep `1b7a`), `begin_service_stop()`, EB activation, `power_off_cmd()`, and `set_mode(...)`. `set_cab(...)` is not in this list: it is manual-only, and `ato.running` is always `False` in manual mode, so there is never an active ATO run for it to disengage (see **ATO run and prior depart**). By the time dwell entry can run, `1b7a` has already cleared `ato.running` on the earlier tick whose Action pass landed the controller in `READY` — the `is_recovery_clean` gate step `3a37` requires — so `enter_station_dwell()` does not itself need to call `ato.stop()`. Resuming ATO after any of these events requires another `depart()` / `ato.go()` acceptance.
- A zero-ATC-clearance hold under live authority is not a run-ending event, so `ato.running` stays `True` and the controller auto-resumes when clearance returns (it is still `RUNNING_MOVING`, per that state's definition). Only the run-ending events listed above clear the flag.
- Manual mode never sets `ato.running`. Neither manual `TrainController.depart()` nor the manual-mode reactive `READY → RUNNING_MOVING` evaluation can make `TrainController.ato.go()` set it; each state move is performed by `OperationalStateMachine.enter_running_moving()` (see the **`TrainController.depart()` canonical contract** and **Reactive condition evaluation**), and `ato.running` stays `False` throughout manual driving.

**Power/cab/mode command contracts**

- `TrainController.commands.power_on_cmd()` is the dedicated `OFF -> powered` transition (`set_mode(...)` always, and `set_cab(...)` in manual mode, also power `OFF → READY` as a side effect — see their command contracts below). It is valid only when power is currently off, and it is processed in the train's Action operator-command slot. When a train starts its transaction `OFF`, `SimulationController` skips that train's route Plan, because planning cannot run before command drain. The Action command slot still runs, so power-on can be accepted. If `power_on_cmd()` succeeds, the controller is no longer `OFF`, so the transaction continues through the remaining powered controller Action logic, voltage output, and normal Action cleanup pass. It does not call `TrainPhysics.tick(...)`: movement first runs in the next tick's Observe batch, and fresh route planning likewise waits for a later Plan tick. The controller transitions to `READY` no matter the cab selection. `power_on_cmd()` does not touch `eb.active`: if EB was latched while the train was `OFF`, the controller lands in `READY` with `eb.active == True` (held at a stand by EB), and the operator clears it with the ordinary `TrainController.eb.release()` from `READY`.
- `TrainController.commands.power_off_cmd()` is valid only while stopped, including with EB latched. `TrainController._apply_power_off_request()` performs the canonical `power_off` writer-helper effects (see the **Latch Table**, row `f8d5`) and writes the power-off/inclusive-cancel latches. Pending power-off then suppresses later propulsion in the same Action.
- `TrainController.complete_power_off()` is the controller-owned OFF-cleanup entry point and canonical `OFF` writer. It transitions `state` to `OFF`, clears the cab through `controller.commands.clear_cab()`, clears EB through `controller.eb.clear()`, calls `controller.ato.stop()`, calls `OperationalStateMachine.reset_handle_to_neutral()`, consumes `ops.service_stop_active` through `TrainController.consume_service_stop(force=True)`, and consumes `pending_power_off` when present. It writes no speed and does not clear the retained manual power percentage: a normally-stopped power-off is already at rest, `SimulationController.clear_failed_runtime()` zeros the speed of a still-rolling ghost train it halts, and the retained percentage is cleared at power-off command time and again on the next powered tick. It is idempotent and valid from any state, including a controller already `OFF`. Its callers are the Action power-off consumer and `SimulationController.clear_failed_runtime()`.
- **Set cab** (`TrainController.commands.set_cab(cab)`) is an operator manual-driving command.
  - **Mode and stopped gate.** Valid only while `control_mode == "manual"` and the train is stopped (`is_stopped() == True`), which includes `RUNNING_AT_STATION` (dwell is a stopped state).
  - **ATO rejection.** In ATO, the controller aligns the cab itself during `TrainController.depart()` (see the **`TrainController.depart()` canonical contract**), so an operator-issued `set_cab` in ATO mode is rejected with a diagnostic such as `"cab selection is only available in manual mode"`. That ATO auto-selection is the system path, separate from this operator command, and is not gated by this rule.
  - **No-op case.** If the requested cab equals the current cab (including a same-letter no-op or `None == None`), `set_cab(...)` is a no-op success: it does NOT change controller state, and it emits no event beyond the ordinary command-result acknowledgement.
  - **No authority side effect.** Otherwise it does not create motion or clear any assigned dispatcher authority.
  - **Reversed-frame re-expression.** Whenever the accepted selection moves the head to the other physical end — `A <-> B`, and equally `None -> B` and `B -> None`, because the head defaults to `end_a` with no cab — the writer that made the change re-expresses the span's two end frames in the reversed travel direction, per the **TrainSpan schema**. This applies identically to all three cab writers: `TrainController.commands.set_cab(...)`, the ATO cab selection inside `TrainController.depart()`, and `TrainController.commands.clear_cab()`.
  - **ATO run and prior depart.** Because the command is manual-only, there is no active ATO run for an operator `set_cab` to disengage (`ato.running` is always `False` in manual mode per the **`ato.running` meaning and lifecycle**), and changing cab invalidates any prior manual depart-acceptance.
  - **State-transition rule.** The result depends on which state `set_cab(...)` is called from:
    - `RUNNING_AT_STATION` with `set_cab(None)` — rejected (`success=False` with a diagnostic such as `"cannot deselect cab while dwelling"`), because `(RUNNING_AT_STATION, None)` is not a legal `(state, cab)` pair per the **Allowed `(state, cab)` pairs** table.
    - `RUNNING_AT_STATION` with a different non-`None` cab letter — accepted; the state stays `RUNNING_AT_STATION` (dwell is preserved; the side effects above still apply).
    - `READY` — the state stays `READY` (only `cab` changes).
    - `OFF`, with the controller already in manual mode — the command powers the controller up to `READY` and applies the cab, because selecting a cab brings a stopped train under control.
    - `RUNNING_MOVING` while the train is actually moving (`is_stopped() == False`) — rejected (`success=False`, for example `"Cannot switch cab while moving"`).
    - `RUNNING_MOVING` while held stopped at the live-authority boundary (`is_stopped() == True`, for example a zero-clearance hold) — the `is_stopped()` precondition is satisfied, so `set_cab(...)` is accepted and transitions the controller to `READY` per the **Controller state machine** table.
  - **Authority mismatch.** If the selected cab points away from the current live authority, the controller must not rewrite that authority. Instead it rebuilds lookahead in the selected travel frame; if that frame has no forward authority, the distance-0 ATC limit becomes `0`, so ATC prevents wrong-direction movement under the mismatched cab choice. A fresh `TrainController.depart()` acceptance is required to re-arm departure.
- **Set mode** (`TrainController.commands.set_mode(mode)`) is valid only while the train is stopped (`is_stopped() == True`), which includes `RUNNING_AT_STATION`. It switches between `ato` and `manual`, disengages any active ATO run by calling `controller.ato.stop()`, clears the retained percentage through `manual.reset_power_percent_for_safety()`, and does not create or clear dispatcher authority. `manual` is a control mode, not a separate operational state.

  The percentage clear keeps a `power_percent` command from surviving a mode change and driving the train when manual `power_percent` is selected again, and it keeps the **driver-control interlock** on `TrainController.eb.release()` reachable: a driver who leaves `power_percent` submode can no longer be holding a percentage they have no accepted command to clear.

  **State-transition rule.** The result depends on which state `set_mode(...)` is called from:
  - `RUNNING_AT_STATION` — the state stays `RUNNING_AT_STATION` (dwell is preserved).
  - `READY` — the state stays `READY`.
  - `RUNNING_MOVING`, possible only while `is_stopped() == True` since the command is rejected while the train is moving — the state transitions to `READY` per the **Controller state machine** table.
  - `OFF` — the command powers the controller up to `READY`.
- `TrainController.commands.set_manual_mode_type(mode_type)` is the canonical setter for `manual.manual_mode_type`. It is valid only while stopped, powered, and in manual control. It never changes operational state. When entering `power_percent`, it calls `OperationalStateMachine.reset_handle_to_neutral()`; when entering `simulation`, it clears the retained percentage through `ManualDriving.reset_power_percent_for_safety()`. It preserves cab and authority and does not start movement.
- **Set handle.** `TrainController.commands.set_handle()` accepts when **all four hold**:
  - `control_mode == manual`
  - `manual_mode_type == simulation`
  - `state != "OFF"`
  - a cab is selected

  Otherwise it returns `success=False`; it is also rejected (`success=False`) when `manual_mode_type == power_percent`.
  - **`EB` position is the exception to these four gates.** When `position == EB`, `set_handle(...)` short-circuits to `TrainController.eb.activate()` and returns before the four gates above, so an `EB` handle activates the emergency brake whatever the submode or cab state — emergency braking must always be reachable. It still requires the train to be powered (the power check runs first, so `set_handle(EB)` on an `OFF` train is rejected); a direct `TrainController.eb.activate()` has no such gate and is valid even while `OFF` (see **EB activation** below).
- **Set manual power percent.** `TrainController.commands.set_manual_power_percent(percent)` accepts under those same driver-input conditions except `manual.manual_mode_type` must be `power_percent` instead of `simulation`. It clamps `percent` to `0..100`, calls `manual.set_power_percent(percent)`, preserves `received_path_plan`, and does not start movement by itself. It is rejected (`success=False`) when `manual_mode_type == simulation` or when any of the shared acceptance preconditions fail.
- **Behavior while EB is latched.** Both commands are still accepted while `eb.active == True`: the operator may move the handle or set any power level, but EB overrides motion. The EB Workflow holds `handle_position` at `EB` for as long as the latch is set, and the zero ATC limit at distance 0 keeps a retained percentage from producing movement. Neither command clears `eb.active`; only `TrainController.eb.release()` releases it, and in `power_percent` submode that release is gated on `manual.manual_power_percent == 0` — so `set_manual_power_percent(0)` is how the driver clears the control before releasing.
- There is no separate `TrainController.set_travel_direction(...)` command in v1. Manual direction selection is only by cab selection through `TrainController.commands.set_cab(...)`.
- **EB activation** (`TrainController.eb.activate()`) is the canonical operator-issued EB command. Its only acceptance gate is `eb.active == False`; a duplicate activation while EB is already latched is rejected as a no-op. On purpose it has no other precondition, because emergency braking must be available at all times: it is valid in any motion state, any operational state including `OFF`, with or without a cab, and with or without a live path.

  On acceptance it performs the **canonical EB activation effects** defined in the **EB workflow state machine**.

- **EB release** (`TrainController.eb.release()`). Accepts when **all six hold**:
  - `state != "OFF"`
  - `eb.active == True`
  - `TrainController.is_stopped() == True`
  - the controller's own `pending_path_cancel_request` is `None` — the EB cancel latch has been consumed
  - the controller's own `received_path_plan` is `None` — the pre-EB authority has transitioned out of `ACTIVE` in `PathDispatcher`
  - the **driver-control interlock** below is satisfied

  When any condition fails, it returns `success=False` and leaves controller state unchanged. The gate reads controller-owned fields plus the controller-facing `received_path_plan` projection; it does not call a dispatcher mutation or inspect a cancelled/inactive path record. The projection's injected active-path reader performs the live `PathDispatcher.get_active_path(train_id)` lookup. The latch conditions prevent same-command-drain EB activation/release from setting recovery latches before Action has committed the EB cancellation.
- **Driver-control interlock.** When `control_mode == "manual"` and `manual.manual_mode_type == "power_percent"`, `TrainController.eb.release()` additionally requires `manual.manual_power_percent == 0`; otherwise it is rejected with a diagnostic such as `"return power to zero before releasing the emergency brake"`. The driver satisfies it with `TrainController.commands.set_manual_power_percent(0)`, which is accepted while `eb.active == True` per the **Power/cab/mode command contracts**. When no cab is selected, `set_manual_power_percent(...)` is rejected by the shared cab precondition; the driver then clears the retained percentage through `TrainController.commands.set_manual_mode_type("simulation")` or `TrainController.commands.set_mode(...)`, both of which reset it through `manual.reset_power_percent_for_safety()`.

  This condition exists because the two manual driver inputs are owned differently while EB is latched: the EB Workflow holds `handle_position` at `EB` for as long as the latch is set, so the handle is already at a braking position when the latch clears, while `manual.manual_power_percent` has no such owner and is set-and-forget per tick step `924d` (Manual-mode command write). Without the interlock, a percentage retained from before or during the EB stop would become the train's command the moment EB cleared, with no fresh driver input. The condition is scoped to the `power_percent` submode because `set_manual_power_percent(...)` is rejected in every other submode. When no cab is selected the same command is also rejected, but `set_manual_mode_type("simulation")` and `set_mode(...)` clear the retained percentage as a general side effect and remain available, so the interlock is always satisfiable by some operator command.

  On acceptance it clears `eb.active` and does not write the operational `state`. The ordinary state owner then applies its normal rule: an existing `RUNNING_AT_STATION` dwell remains in that route-owned state, while any other powered, stopped, authority-free controller satisfies the ordinary reactive transition to `READY`. Dwell timing fields are untouched because neither EB activation nor release owns route timing.

**EB workflow state machine**

This is the single canonical step-by-step contract for EB activation, release, and post-EB restart in v1. Shared contracts must not invent separate EB-recovery state flags on `TrainController` or `RouteExecutor` beyond the ones listed below.

**Canonical EB activation effects** (referenced elsewhere by name). On activation:
- Sets `eb.active = True`.
- Forces handle to `EB`.
- Calls `controller.ato.stop()`.
- Clears the `ops.service_stop_active` latch through `TrainController.consume_service_stop()`.
- When a live path exists, calls `PhaseLatches.set_path_cancel_request(error=<ErrorRecord origin "eb">, kind="warning")` (see the Latch Table for overwrite behavior).

Other sites must cross-reference this paragraph by name and must not restate the effect list.

EB is a controller condition, not a separate route workflow. While `eb.active` is true, every Plan branch that would create/extend authority, complete dwell, or depart is ineligible. Existing timers may continue to measure their documented clocks, but their state-changing completion waits until the condition clears. Activation with no live path naturally writes no cancellation request because the general activation effect is conditional on live authority; no dwell-specific activation branch is needed.

| Step | Trigger | Actor | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 (`4c64`). EB activation | ATC overspeed escalation (including the zero-limit branch in step `826a`) or the operator-issued `TrainController.eb.activate()` command | `TrainController.tick()` (Action): operator EB is accepted during the command drain; ATC EB is raised later in control evaluation | Both triggers run `TrainController.eb.activate()`. A command-drain cancellation may reach the early dispatcher slot in this pass; an ATC-written request occurs after that slot and waits for the next Action pass. In either case the stopped gate keeps authority until the train stops, then dispatcher cancellation commits or no-ops if authority already ended. Ordinary tick work remains under EB until explicit release. |
| 2 (`e67d`). Rolling stop under EB | Physics integrates EB deceleration | `TrainPhysics.tick()` | In ATO and manual `simulation` submode, the train decelerates according to `SpeedProfile.emergency_brake_rate`; in manual `power_percent` submode the momentum-free model writes the capped zero speed the same tick instead, per **Canonical power-percent safety-cap ordering** (`emergency_brake_rate` does not apply there). `current_span` and `current_speed_kmh` continue to update normally either way. No additional authority completion/cancellation side effects fire during rolling beyond the earlier EB-cancellation request, but physics remains authoritative: `TrainPhysics.tick(...)` continues emitting span updates, and the same train's Observe pass continues committing physical entry and tail-vacate resource updates while EB is latched. |
| 3 (`9f74`). Full stop under EB | `TrainController.is_stopped()` returns `True` | `TrainController.tick()` | Controller remains in the EB early-exit loop with `eb.active == True`; no state transition yet. Dispatcher path completion cannot commit while `eb.active == True`, and no condition in the **Stop-arrival check** says so: EB activation latched `pending_path_cancel_request` per the **canonical EB activation effects**, and step `9d8b` skips the arrival check entirely while that latch is set. |
| 4 (`ad04`). EB release | `TrainController.eb.release()` called while stopped and powered after any EB cancellation latch has been consumed, no live authority remains, and the **driver-control interlock** is satisfied | operator | Clears `eb.active = False` and writes no operational state. Existing route/controller state then follows its ordinary transition rules. The command does not call `RouteExecutor`, inspect or complete a cancelled path, or clear route-owned recovery state. |
| 5 (`29a0`). Ordinary cancellation recovery | `RouteRun.path_cancelled == True` and `controller.is_recovery_clean` is true on the next eligible `RouteExecutor.tick_train_plan(...)` | `RouteExecutor.tick_train_plan(...)` (Plan) | The ordinary Plan route-deviation-cleanup step clears `RouteRun.path_cancelled`; Plan then continues through covered-task advance, `RouteExecutor._find_next_task_target(train_id)`, and fresh `PathDispatcher.create_path(...)`, then writes `phase_latches.departure_request` when eligible (the Action transition consumer calls `TrainController.depart()`). This row is used for every recoverable cancellation, including one requested by EB; it contains no EB-only restart path. |

- `eb.active` is controller-owned, but EB activation must request dispatcher cancellation through `pending_path_cancel_request` immediately when a live path exists. The actual cancellation side effects still run only inside `PathDispatcher` during the same train's later Action consume pass; `TrainController` never releases resources itself.
- EB recovery uses the same recovery latches as any other cancellation: `RouteRun.path_cancelled` for route-owned recovery cleanup. No EB-specific route hook or auto-depart flag exists in v1.
- `eb.active` while `OFF`: `TrainController.eb.activate()` is accepted in `OFF` and latches `eb.active = True` with no live path to cancel. The latch survives `OFF → READY`: `power_on_cmd()` does not clear it, so a train powered on with EB latched rests in `(state == READY, eb.active == True)`, held at a stand by EB, until the operator issues the ordinary `TrainController.eb.release()` from `READY` (row `ad04`). There is no separate OFF-state EB clear path; `eb.release()` is rejected while `OFF` per its `state != "OFF"` gate.

**received_path_plan schema**

- This is the single canonical schema for the controller's active path-plan payload. Every producer/consumer must refer back to this subsection by name instead of restating the field list elsewhere.
- **Why this shape.** The controller's job is to brake to the live authority boundary using its safety margin and to compute speed restrictions live from the network and the authorized corridor. That work needs the corridor geometry (`resource_sequence`) and the boundary (`authority_end_block_id`); it does not need the requested target the create/extend call carried, which the **Stop-arrival check** reads route-side. Keeping the projection narrow lets the controller stay decoupled from dispatcher-side completion logic and lets `received_path_plan` regenerate as a pure read with no caching.
- `received_path_plan` carries exactly `path_id`, `resource_sequence`, and `authority_end_block_id` in v1. It is the controller's only active path-plan payload. `resource_sequence` uses the canonical **resource_sequence entry schema**, and each nested `path_tiles` slice uses the canonical **path_tile entry schema**, so the controller can extend lookahead along the actual geometry without inferring terminal-frame direction from tile coordinates alone. The requested target (`requested_destination_block_id`, `requested_destination_direction`) is a `PathDispatcher.create_path(...)` / `extend_path(...)` argument recorded route-side on `RouteRun.task_runs[i].resolved_target` (per **Path field schema**), never stored on the `Path` record and never in `received_path_plan`; the controller does not see those fields.
